generatedFrom: command-catalog.v1.1.json (frozen), plus E0 catalog v2: ParamRef target widening, routing DAG commands, project phase anchor, and the eight deferred contract proposals. See DESIGN-catalog-v2.md. E1 adds note-backed clips and the MIDI note commands (new names only).

commands.name: project.new
commands.nonUndoableReason: Lifecycle action that creates the .mstudio package; there is no prior project state to invert into. Runs through the command bus for uniform UI/MCP/agent access but is not a journal entry.

name.description: Display name for the new project; also the .mstudio package's name on disk. Non-empty. This is a NAME, not a path — project.open is the one that takes a path.

commands.description: Create a new .mstudio package on disk with an empty timeline. Initial tempo/timeSig/key are set by follow-up project.setTempo/setTimeSig/setKey commands so those mutations are uniformly journaled.

commands.name: project.open
commands.nonUndoableReason: Session action (loads a package into memory); does not mutate project content.

path.description: Filesystem path to an existing .mstudio package directory. Non-empty, and the package must already exist: this command never creates one.

commands.description: Open an existing .mstudio package: read project.json (checkpoint), replay any journal segment newer than the checkpoint, and hydrate the in-memory model.

commands.name: project.save
commands.nonUndoableReason: Checkpoint action, not a content mutation. Its effect is the project.json-checkpoint-plus-journal-truncation-marker sequence described in 02-ARCHITECTURE.md section 6, which is orthogonal to the per-edit journal this schema validates.
commands.description: Write project.json as a checkpoint of the current journal tip and mark prior journal segments eligible for truncation once the write is durable.

commands.name: project.setTempo

bpm.description: Tempo in beats per minute, greater than 0 and at most 999. Journaled as a Num, so the integer/float SHAPE is part of the hash chain: send 120, not 120.0, unless you mean a fractional tempo.

commands.description: Set the project's global tempo in beats per minute. v1 has one tempo for the whole project (no tempo map / tempo automation).

commands.name: project.setTimeSig

numerator.description: Beats per bar — the TOP number of 4/4 — from 1 to 32.

denominator.description: Beat unit — the BOTTOM number of 4/4 — one of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 or 32.

commands.description: Set the bar length the grid, ruler and metronome count in, e.g. 4/4 or 6/8. One signature for the whole project in v1 — there is no signature map.

commands.name: project.setKey

key.description: Key and scale as '<root> <mode>', e.g. 'C major' or 'A minor'. Root is A-G with an optional '#' or 'b'; mode is 'major' or 'minor'. Matches the keyscale vocabulary ace_generator.py already uses. Metadata only — note content is not checked against it.

commands.description: Set the project's key/scale metadata (informational for v1; not enforced against note content).

commands.name: section.set

sectionId.description: Caller-minted, stable id for the section; the engine never mints one. A fresh id CREATES a section, an existing id UPDATES it (this command is an upsert).

name.description: Section label shown in the arrangement ruler, e.g. 'Verse', 'Chorus', 'Bridge' or 'Drop'. Non-empty.

startTicks.description: Where the section begins, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar).

color.description: Optional swatch, '#RRGGBB' hex with six digits and no alpha (e.g. '#FF8800'). Omitted leaves the section with no explicit colour.

commands.description: Create or update a named arrangement section marker. Catalog default inverse is section.remove (correct for the create case); when section.set updates an EXISTING sectionId's fields, the runtime executor uses a self-inverse (section.set with the prior name/startTicks/color) instead. See engine/contracts/README.md open question: this is an upsert command with a context-dependent inverse, which a static per-command inverseRule cannot fully express.

commands.name: section.remove

sectionId.description: Id of an existing section. Removing an id that is not there is a typed error, not a silent no-op.

commands.description: Delete an arrangement section marker. Only the label goes — no audio, clip or track is touched.

commands.name: marker.set

markerId.description: Caller-minted, stable id for the marker; the engine never mints one. A fresh id CREATES a marker, an existing id UPDATES it (this command is an upsert).

positionTicks.description: Marker position, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar).

label.description: Text drawn on the marker in the ruler, e.g. 'Solo starts'. Non-empty.

color.description: Optional swatch, '#RRGGBB' hex with six digits and no alpha (e.g. '#FF8800'). Omitted leaves the marker with no explicit colour.

commands.description: Create or update a timeline marker. Catalog default inverse is marker.remove (correct for the create case; P0-C proposal 1, APPROVED by the coordinating session 2026-07-11, mirroring section.set/section.remove); when marker.set updates an EXISTING markerId's fields, the runtime executor uses a self-inverse (marker.set with the prior positionTicks/label/color) instead, the same upsert nuance as section.set.

commands.name: marker.remove

markerId.description: Id of an existing marker. Removing an id that is not there is a typed error, not a silent no-op.

commands.description: Remove a timeline marker. Added as marker.set's undo-completing counterpart (P0-C proposal 1, APPROVED by the coordinating session 2026-07-11), mirroring section.remove.

commands.name: transport.play
commands.description: Start playback from the current transport position. Unjournaled per 02-ARCH section 4: transport commands are real commands on the bus but never appear in journal.jsonl.

commands.name: transport.stop
commands.description: Stop playback and leave the playhead exactly where it stopped. Use transport.seek afterwards to move it. Unjournaled per 02-ARCH section 4.

commands.name: transport.seek

positionTicks.description: Where to put the playhead, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar). Seeking past the end of the material is allowed.

commands.description: Jump the playhead to a position without starting or stopping playback. Unjournaled per 02-ARCH section 4.

commands.name: transport.loop.set

startTicks.description: Loop start, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar). Must be strictly BEFORE endTicks; equal or inverted is refused, so a zero-length loop cannot be set.

endTicks.description: Loop end, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar). Must be strictly AFTER startTicks.

commands.description: Mark the region the transport should loop over. Start must be strictly before end, so a zero-length loop cannot be set. Unjournaled view/transport state.

commands.name: transport.loop.clear
commands.description: Turn looping off and leave the transport playing straight through. Unjournaled view/transport state.

commands.name: transport.metronome

enabled.description: true starts the click, false stops it. Absolute, not a toggle: sending true twice leaves the click on.

commands.description: Toggle the metronome click. v1 metronome is a simple click, no accent patterns or sound choices.

commands.name: track.add

trackId.description: Caller-minted, stable id for the new track; the engine never mints one, because a minted id would make replay diverge from the live model. An id already in use is refused, never merged.

name.description: Display name on the track header, e.g. 'Lead Vocal'. Non-empty, need not be unique, and is NOT the identity — trackId is.

index.description: Optional 0-based insert position; 0 makes it the first track. May equal the current track count (append), and anything larger is refused. Omitted appends.

commands.description: Create an empty track to put clips, an instrument or effects on. The id is yours to mint and is permanent; index optionally places it in the list, otherwise it is appended.

commands.name: track.remove

trackId.description: Id of the track to delete. Every clip, device, effect, send and automation lane on it goes too, and undo restores all of them.

commands.description: Delete a track along with every clip, device, effect, send and automation lane on it. Undo restores all of it, so this is reversible; the audio assets under audio/ are content-addressed and are not deleted.

commands.name: track.rename

trackId.description: Id of the track to rename. The id itself never changes — it is the wire identity for the life of the project.

name.description: New display name for the track. Non-empty.

commands.description: Change the display name a person sees on a track header. The trackId is unaffected: ids are the wire identity and never change, so every clip, lane and binding that names this track keeps working.

commands.name: track.reorder

trackId.description: Id of the track to move.

newIndex.description: 0-based destination slot. Must be strictly LESS than the current track count — unlike track.add's index, which may equal it.

commands.description: Move a track to a different slot in the track list. Display order only: it changes nothing about routing or the mix.

commands.name: track.setColor

trackId.description: Id of the track being recoloured.

color.description: Track colour as '#RRGGBB' hex: six hex digits, leading '#' required, no alpha channel (e.g. '#3AA6FF').

commands.description: Give a track a colour in the timeline and mixer, so an arrangement can be read at a glance. Display only — it changes nothing about the audio.

commands.name: track.setHeight

trackId.description: Id of the track whose lane height changes.

heightPx.description: Lane height in points, 24 to 400. Purely how tall the lane is drawn; it changes nothing about the audio.

commands.description: Set how tall a track's lane is drawn in the timeline, e.g. to give the one you are editing more room. Display only.

commands.name: track.mute

trackId.description: Id of the track to mute or unmute.

muted.description: true silences the track in playback and in every bounce, false unmutes it. Absolute, not a toggle.

commands.description: Silence a whole track, or bring it back. Absolute rather than a toggle, so it is safe to send the same value twice; the state is journaled and undoable, and it is honoured by playback and by the master bounce.

commands.name: track.solo

trackId.description: Id of the track to solo or unsolo.

soloed.description: true solos the track (only soloed tracks are heard), false unsolos. Absolute, not a toggle. Honoured by the master bounce and deliberately IGNORED by stem export, which always writes every track.

commands.description: Hear one track (or a set of them) on its own by silencing everything not soloed. Honoured by playback and the master bounce, and deliberately IGNORED by stem export, which always writes every track.

commands.name: track.arm

trackId.description: Id of the track to arm. record.start captures onto armed tracks.

armed.description: true arms the track for recording, false disarms. Absolute, not a toggle. Arming alone never opens the microphone — record.start or record.inputListen does.

commands.description: Arm or disarm a track for recording. The armed track is the capture target for record.start; arming is journaled and undoable. Arming does not open the microphone — that happens at record.start (or opt-in record.inputListen).

commands.name: track.setInputChannel

trackId.description: Id of the audio track whose hardware input assignment changes.

channel.description: 0-based hardware input channel this track records from: channel 0 is the first input on the interface. On a four-input box, set 0, 1, 2, 3 across four armed tracks and one pass lands each channel on its own track.

commands.description: Choose which hardware input channel an audio track records from. On a four-input interface (e.g. Zoom AMS-44), set track 1 to channel 0, track 2 to channel 1, and so on, arm all four, and record once — each track lands its own channel. Journaled and undoable.

commands.name: device.add

trackId.description: Id of the track that will host the instrument. Give a track only ONE device: a second device is accepted here (only a duplicate deviceId is refused) but the render compile then hard-errors, because the baked note lane is per track and a second instrument would have no notes to play.

deviceId.description: Opaque device id. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> stays parseable.

kind.description: Which instrument to build: 'synth' (the four-waveform subtractive synth), 'sampler' (pitched, zone-mapped audio) or 'drum' (one pad per key). The E2 instrument vocabulary, and CLOSED — an unknown kind fails at the contract boundary.

commands.description: Add an instrument to a track. Its parameters become automatable IMMEDIATELY through the existing ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> — no contract change, which is what E0 3 promised. A NEW command name (E0 9.2).

commands.name: device.remove

trackId.description: Id of the track the instrument sits on.

deviceId.description: Opaque device id. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> stays parseable.

commands.description: Remove an instrument from a track. Refused if the device carries stored parameters this build has no command to restore, so removing it is always undoable.

commands.name: device.zone.add

trackId.description: Id of the track the sampler/drum device sits on.

deviceId.description: Opaque device id. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> stays parseable.

zoneId.description: Opaque, stable zone id. Identity for edit and undo.

sourceId.description: Content-addressed asset id — the SAME registry clip.place's assetHash names. Resolved render-side through the same loaded-source map, with the same loud 'references unloaded source' failure.

rootPitch.description: The MIDI note the recording sounds at, 0 to 127; a sampler reads at 2^((pitch-rootPitch)/12). Ignored by kind 'drum', which does not pitch-track.

loPitch.description: Lowest MIDI key the zone covers, 0 to 127.

hiPitch.description: Highest MIDI key the zone covers, 0 to 127. Must be >= loPitch, and must EQUAL loPitch on a 'drum' device, because a pad is one key.

gainDb.description: Optional zone/pad gain in dB. Default 0, which is unity.

pan.description: Optional pad pan, -1 is hard left and 1 is hard right; default 0 is centre. Honoured by kind 'drum'; IGNORED by 'sampler', which is a pitched instrument sitting on the track's own pan.

commands.description: Bind an audio source to a sampler zone or a drum pad. This is what makes kind 'sampler' and kind 'drum' reachable at all: Device.params is Num-only and could never name an asset. A NEW command name (E0 9.2) — device.add is deliberately NOT widened with an optional sourceId, because replay does not validate params and an older binary would verify the chain and then silently build a sampler with no audio.

commands.name: device.zone.remove

trackId.description: Id of the track the sampler/drum device sits on.

deviceId.description: Opaque device id. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> stays parseable.

commands.description: Remove one source binding from a sampler or drum device. The inverse carries every field the zone held, gain and pan included, so remove+add is exact. Refused if the zone carries unknown fields this build has no command to restore. There is no device.zone.set: an edit is remove+add, which keeps every inverse exact without inventing per-field defaults.

commands.name: device.param.set

trackId.description: Id of the track the instrument sits on.

deviceId.description: Opaque device id. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> stays parseable.

key.description: An instrument parameter key from DEVICE_PARAM_KEYS — the SAME token the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> already carries, so a value authored here and a lane automating it name the parameter identically. Which keys a given kind honours is deliberately NOT validated: apply.rs runs on replay, so tightening the (kind, key) pairing later would break replay of a project that authored a key its kind ignores (a drum rack ignores 'waveform'; every kind but 'synth' ignores it).

value.description: Parameter value. Journaled as a Num, so the integer/float SHAPE round-trips exactly.

commands.description: Set one instrument parameter — the waveform an oscillator runs, its filter cutoff, its ADSR envelope. This is the setter E1/E2 deliberately omitted ("its inverse cannot be exact without per-parameter defaults that the DSP lane owns"); E5 answered that for fx.param.set and this is the same answer for Device: parameters stay SPARSE, an absent key means the DSP default exactly as build_instrument already implements it, so the inverse of setting an ABSENT key is device.param.clear and no default is ever materialized into the project. inverseShape is 'multi' because the declared inverse name cannot cover both directions. A NEW command name (E0 9.2) — device.add is deliberately NOT widened with optional params, because replay does not validate params and an older binary would verify the chain and then silently build an instrument with a different sound.

commands.name: device.param.clear

trackId.description: Id of the track the instrument sits on.

deviceId.description: Opaque device id. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> stays parseable.

key.description: An instrument parameter key from DEVICE_PARAM_KEYS — the SAME token the ParamRef path track.device.<deviceId>.<paramKey> already carries, so a value authored here and a lane automating it name the parameter identically. Which keys a given kind honours is deliberately NOT validated: apply.rs runs on replay, so tightening the (kind, key) pairing later would break replay of a project that authored a key its kind ignores (a drum rack ignores 'waveform'; every kind but 'synth' ignores it).

commands.description: Drop one stored instrument parameter, restoring sparsity so the key reads as the DSP default again. Clearing a key that stores no value is a typed error, not a silent no-op: a no-op has no exact inverse to journal.

commands.name: record.start

trackId.description: The armed track to capture onto.

deviceId.description: Optional input device name to open. Omitted opens the system default input.

startTicks.description: With punchOutTicks, the punch-in position. Otherwise, when stopped, the position where the take lands after snapping to the anchored bar grid; while rolling without a punch it is ignored. Default: the capture origin.

punchOutTicks.description: Punch-out position. When set, record.stop lands a clip of exactly punchOutTicks minus startTicks (the punch region), truncating or silence-padding the capture to fit. Omitted means open-ended capture until record.stop.

commands.description: Begin capturing from an audio input onto an armed track. The host reports captureOriginTicks and rolling from the actual input-ready transport clock; while rolling, an omitted startTicks records at the live playhead and a supplied startTicks is ignored unless punchOutTicks defines a punch region. Opens an INPUT-only stream and never an output stream; monitoring stays silent. Unjournaled transport-class action: the take and clip landed by record.stop are the journaled, undoable unit.

commands.name: record.rotate
commands.description: Complete the current loop-record pass without stopping or reopening the input stream. The host rotates the writer-side capture accumulator, immediately continues filling the next pass, and prepares the completed pass asynchronously before committing its atomic record transaction. No-op when nothing is recording.

commands.name: record.stop
commands.description: Stop the active capture and land the recorded audio as a candidate take and a placed clip with human-origin lineage (txn.begin / gen.landed sourceCommand record.commit / clip.place / txn.commit). No-op when nothing is recording.

commands.name: record.cancel
commands.description: Discard the active capture without landing a take or clip. No-op when nothing is recording.

commands.name: record.inputListen

enabled.description: true opens the input for metering only (no landing); false closes it. Does not enable speaker monitoring.

deviceId.description: Optional input device name to open. Omitted opens the system default input.

commands.description: Opt-in input listen for gain-staging and per-channel metering WITHOUT recording. Arming a track never opens the mic; this command (or record.start) does. The snapshot reports inputOpen so the UI can show when an input is live. Monitoring (hearing yourself through speakers) stays double-gated and is not enabled by this command.

commands.name: midi.device.select
commands.nonUndoableReason: Selects or pins which MIDI input port a map is bound to. Port binding is session/device state, not project content, so it is neither journaled nor replayable; undo would have nothing in the project model to restore.

device.description: Reported port name, e.g. 'USB MIDI Interface'.

map.description: Optional map key (file stem or map name) to pin to this port, 'none' to leave the port unmapped, or 'auto' to go back to pattern auto-detect. Omitted leaves the current selection alone.

commands.description: Pin a specific control map to a MIDI input port, or hand it back to auto-detect. Reach for this when a controller is being matched to the wrong map.

commands.name: midi.port.role.set
commands.nonUndoableReason: Chooses whether a MIDI input port's NOTE messages play the selected instrument or fire the port's control bindings. Port role is session/device state, not project content, so it is neither journaled nor replayable; undo would have nothing in the project model to restore.

port.description: Reported port name, e.g. 'USB MIDI Interface'.

role.description: instrument (the DEFAULT): note messages play the selected instrument track and are recordable; the port's note-matched control bindings are suppressed, while its CC/pitch-bend bindings still fire. control: every binding fires and notes never sound.

commands.description: Set what a MIDI input port's KEYS do: play the instrument (default) or drive its control bindings.

commands.name: midi.learn.start
commands.nonUndoableReason: Opens a transient learn session. It mutates no project state; closing it again is midi.learn.stop, not an undo.

device.description: Optional port name to scope capture to, e.g. 'USB MIDI Interface'. Omitted takes the first control from any device.

commands.description: Begin listening for the next control a person touches, so the following midi.binding.set can bind it without anyone having to know its channel and CC number.

commands.name: midi.learn.stop
commands.nonUndoableReason: Closes a transient learn session. It mutates no project state; the binding it may have produced is undone by midi.binding.clear, not by inverting this.
commands.description: Stop listening for a control. Any binding the session produced stays: it is undone with midi.binding.clear, not by closing the session.

commands.name: midi.binding.set
commands.nonUndoableReason: Writes the user's controller overlay map to the app directory, which is machine configuration outside the .mstudio package. midi.binding.clear removes a binding explicitly; the undo stack never crosses out of the project.

device.description: Optional port name whose resolved map takes the binding. Omitted uses the learn session's captured device.

type.description: Which MIDI message class the binding matches: 'noteOn', 'noteOff', 'controlChange' or 'pitchBend'.

channel.description: MIDI channel to match, 0-BASED: 0 to 15. Channel 1 on the hardware is 0 here.

number.description: Note or CC number to match, 0 to 127. Optional, and omitted for pitchBend, which is channel-wide.

control.description: Optional explicit control coordinates (type, channel, and number for note/CC). Omitted uses the learn session's captured control.

kind.description: Which target family this is: 'command' (a catalog command by name), 'builtin' (a named built-in action) or 'sterling' (instruction text queued for the copilot).

name.description: The action to run: with kind 'command' a catalog command name, with kind 'builtin' one of the built-in action names. Optional for kind 'sterling', which uses instruction instead.

params.description: Optional params template for kind 'command'. May carry the '$value' placeholder (the mapped control value) and '$track:N' (the Nth track's id).

instruction.description: Instruction text queued for the Sterling copilot. Required for kind 'sterling', optional and ignored otherwise.

target.description: What firing this control DOES. kind 'command' submits a catalog command (name + a params template that may carry the '$value' and '$track:N' placeholders), 'builtin' runs a named built-in action, 'sterling' queues instruction text for the Sterling copilot.

inputMin.description: Raw controller value treated as the low end, 0 to 127. Default 0.

inputMax.description: Raw controller value treated as the high end, 0 to 127. Default 127.

outputMin.description: Value produced at inputMin, in the TARGET parameter's own units (dB for a gain, -1..1 for a pan). Default 0.

outputMax.description: Value produced at inputMax, in the TARGET parameter's own units. Default 1.

curve.description: How input maps onto output between the two ends: 'linear', 'exponential' or 'logarithmic'. Default 'linear'.

valueMap.description: Optional scaling from the controller's raw reading to the value the target receives. Omitted, the raw is normalized to 0..1 and handed over as-is.

label.description: Optional human-readable name for the binding, shown in MIDI settings. Omitted leaves it unlabelled.

enabled.description: Whether the binding fires at all. Default true; false keeps it on file without it acting.

commands.description: Bind a physical knob, pad or key to a Studio action and persist it, so a controller can drive commands. Usually issued right after midi.learn.start captures the control.

commands.name: midi.binding.clear
commands.nonUndoableReason: Removes a binding from the user's controller overlay map, which is machine configuration outside the .mstudio package. Restoring it is an explicit midi.binding.set, not an undo step.

device.description: Reported MIDI port name whose user overlay map holds the binding, e.g. 'USB MIDI Interface'.

type.description: Which MIDI message class the binding matched: 'noteOn', 'noteOff', 'controlChange' or 'pitchBend'.

channel.description: MIDI channel the binding matched, 0-BASED: 0 to 15.

number.description: Note or CC number the binding matched, 0 to 127. Omitted for pitchBend, which is channel-wide.

control.description: The exact control coordinates of the binding to drop — the same type/channel/number shape midi.binding.set matched on. There are no wildcards: a binding is cleared by naming it exactly.

commands.description: Drop one binding from a port's user overlay map, so that control goes back to doing nothing (or to whatever the bundled map says).

commands.name: midi.map.import
commands.nonUndoableReason: Copies a map file into the user maps directory. Filesystem I/O outside the project package, in the same class as export.*: not journaled, not invertible.

sourcePath.description: Filesystem path of the MIDI map file to bring in. It is COPIED into the user maps directory, so later edits to the original have no effect.

overwrite.description: Optional. true replaces an existing user map with the same file name; false (the default) refuses rather than clobbering it.

commands.description: Copy a MIDI map file someone else wrote into the user maps directory so this install can resolve ports against it. The file is copied, not linked.

commands.name: midi.map.export
commands.nonUndoableReason: Writes a map file to a path outside the app directory. Filesystem I/O outside the project package, in the same class as export.*: not journaled, not invertible.

map.description: Map key (file stem or map name).

outputPath.description: Filesystem path to write the map file to. Manage tier: this writes outside the app's own directories, so the tool also needs confirm: true.

commands.description: Write a MIDI map out verbatim to a path of your choosing, e.g. to share it or check it into a repository. Manage tier because it writes outside the app's directories.

commands.name: midi.reload
commands.nonUndoableReason: Re-reads maps from disk and re-resolves ports. Idempotent refresh of device state with no prior project state to restore.
commands.description: Re-read every bundled and user MIDI map from disk and re-resolve the connected ports against them — what to call after editing a map file by hand.

commands.name: clip.place

clipId.description: Caller-minted, stable id for the new clip; the engine never mints one. Must not already be in use anywhere in the project.

trackId.description: Id of the track to place the clip on. Clips on one track may NOT overlap — an overlapping placement is refused, not nudged.

assetHash.description: blake3 hash of the audio asset under audio/: 64 lowercase hex characters. The asset must already be in the package — this command references, it does not import.

startTicks.description: Where the clip starts on the timeline, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar).

lengthTicks.description: How long the clip is, in ticks. The schema admits 0 for historical reasons but the executor REFUSES it: this must be greater than 0.

sourceOffsetTicks.description: Optional offset INTO the asset at which the clip starts reading, in ticks. Default 0 (play from the top of the file). offset + length must stay inside the asset's extent.

commands.description: Put an existing content-addressed audio asset on a track as a clip. The asset must already be in the package (import.audio is what brings one in); clips on a track may not overlap.

commands.name: clip.placeMidi

clipId.description: Caller-minted, stable id for the new note clip; the engine never mints one. Must not already be in use anywhere in the project.

trackId.description: Id of the track to place the clip on. Clips on one track may NOT overlap — an overlapping placement is refused.

startTicks.description: Where the clip starts on the timeline, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar).

lengthTicks.description: How long the clip is, in ticks; must be greater than 0. Note positions are CLIP-RELATIVE, so this is the window they live in.

commands.description: Place an empty NOTE-BACKED (MIDI) clip on a track. A NEW command name, not an optional param on clip.place: catalog v2 design 9.2 — replay does not validate params, so an older binary would verify the chain and silently build a wrong model, whereas an unknown command name hard-fails the open.

commands.name: clip.move

clipId.description: Id of the clip to move.

trackId.description: Destination track; equal to the clip's current track for a same-lane move.

startTicks.description: New clip start, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar). The destination must be clear — clips on one track may not overlap.

commands.description: Move a clip to a new start position, optionally onto a different track. This is the exact command shown as the worked example in 02-ARCHITECTURE.md section 4.

commands.name: clip.trim

clipId.description: Id of the clip to trim.

edge.description: Which edge moves: 'start' or 'end'. 'start' is REFUSED on a note-backed clip (it would shift every note relative to the clip); 'end' works on audio and note clips alike.

deltaTicks.description: Signed tick delta, and it may not be 0. On the 'start' edge a positive value shortens from the front (the start moves later); on the 'end' edge a positive value lengthens. The result must leave a length greater than 0 and must not collide with a neighbouring clip.

commands.description: Move one edge of a clip to crop or extend it, without moving the audio inside it. Delta-based and self-inverse. The start edge is refused on a note-backed clip.

commands.name: clip.split

clipId.description: Id of the clip to split. It becomes the LEFT piece and keeps this id; the right piece gets newClipId.

atTicks.description: Split point, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar), STRICTLY inside the clip: after its start and before its end. A split exactly on an edge is refused rather than silently ignored.

newClipId.description: Caller-minted id for the RIGHT-hand piece the split creates; must not already be in use. The left piece keeps the original clipId.

commands.description: Cut one clip into two at a point strictly inside it. The left piece keeps the original id, the right piece takes newClipId, and no audio is re-encoded.

commands.name: clip.duplicate

clipId.description: Id of the clip to copy. The original is untouched.

newClipId.description: Caller-minted id for the copy; must not already be in use.

startTicks.description: Where the copy starts, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar). The copy always lands on the SOURCE clip's own track — this command carries no destination track — so that span must be clear.

commands.description: Copy a clip and place the copy at another position on the SAME track — despite what earlier wording implied, this command carries no destination track and cannot move a copy to another lane. Use clip.duplicate then clip.move for that.

commands.name: clip.remove

clipId.description: Id of the clip to remove from the timeline. The underlying audio asset under audio/ is NOT deleted: it is content-addressed and other clips may reference it.

commands.description: Remove a clip from the timeline. The underlying audio asset is not deleted (content-addressed, may be referenced elsewhere).

commands.name: clip.setGain

clipId.description: Id of the clip whose trim changes.

gainDb.description: Clip gain trim in dB, -60 to 12; 0 is unity. Applied ON TOP OF the track fader (mix.gain), not instead of it. The bound is enforced by the executor, not only by this schema.

commands.description: Trim one clip's level without touching the channel fader, so a single quiet line can be brought up inside an otherwise balanced mix.

commands.name: clip.mute

clipId.description: Id of the clip to mute or unmute.

muted.description: true silences just this clip, false unmutes it. Absolute, not a toggle, and independent of track.mute.

commands.description: Silence one clip while leaving the rest of its track audible — the usual way to drop a bad line out of a comp without deleting it.

commands.name: clip.fade.set

clipId.description: Id of the clip whose fade changes.

edge.description: Which fade this sets: 'in' (the clip's head) or 'out' (its tail).

lengthTicks.description: Fade length in ticks, 0 or more; 0 removes the fade. The fade may not be longer than the clip — a trim or split that would leave it hanging over the edge is refused instead.

shape.description: Fade curve: 'linear', 'equalPower', 'exponential' or 'logarithmic'. equalPower holds perceived loudness roughly constant and is the usual choice where two clips meet.

commands.description: Shape the head or tail of a clip so it does not start or stop abruptly, or remove an existing fade by setting its length to 0.

commands.name: clip.crossfade.set

clipIdA.description: Id of the EARLIER clip of the adjacent pair. Both clips must sit on the same track.

clipIdB.description: Id of the LATER clip of the adjacent pair.

lengthTicks.description: Crossfade length in ticks, 0 or more; 0 means no crossfade. Required rather than optional by the self-inverse rule — the pre-state of a joint's FIRST crossfade is 'none', and the inverse has to be able to say so.

commands.description: Blend the joint between two adjacent clips on one track so the seam is inaudible, or remove an existing crossfade by setting its length to 0.

commands.name: clip.warp.set

clipId.description: Id of the clip whose time-warp changes.

mode.description: 'ratio' applies the fixed stretchRatio you supply and is the mode that does something. 'conform' is accepted and journaled, but this build resolves it to whatever stretchRatio the clip already carried: conform-to-project-tempo needs a stored SOURCE tempo the engine does not have yet (E7 warp markers), so it is not a tempo match today.

stretchRatio.description: Playback stretch factor, greater than 0; 1.0 is unwarped and 2.0 plays at half speed. Optional at the top level of this schema but REQUIRED when mode is 'ratio' (the if/then branch pins it), and meaningless when mode is 'conform'. The renderer clamps what it can actually stretch to 0.25x..4x.

commands.description: Set how a clip's audio is stretched against the timeline: a fixed ratio, or 'conform', which this build resolves to the ratio the clip already carried rather than matching the project tempo (see the mode parameter).

commands.name: clip.phaseAnchor.set

clipId.description: Id of the clip whose bar-grid phase anchor changes.

anchorTicks.description: Where this clip's warped source considers the bar grid to begin, in ticks, 0 or more. 0 is the unshifted default.

commands.description: Tell a warped clip where its own bar grid begins, so a performance with a lead-in locks to the bars a person sees rather than to tick 0.

commands.name: clip.rename

clipId.description: Id of the clip to relabel. Its id does not change — only the label a person sees.

name.description: New display label for the clip. Non-empty.

commands.description: Change the label drawn on a clip. The clipId is unaffected — ids are the wire identity and never change.

commands.name: note.add

clipId.description: Id of a NOTE-BACKED clip (one made by clip.placeMidi). Rejected on an audio clip.

noteId.description: Note identity, unique within its clip. Minted UI-SIDE (ULID-shaped), exactly like autopoint.add's pointId — the engine never mints an id at apply time, because a minted id would make replay diverge from the live model.

lengthTicks.description: Sounding length in ticks. Must be > 0.

pitch.description: MIDI note number, 0 to 127; 60 is middle C. The engine never clamps — a batch that would leave the range is refused whole.

velocity.description: MIDI velocity, 0 to 127. Send it as an INTEGER literal: it is journaled as a Num, whose integer/float shape the blake3 chain depends on, so 100 and 100.0 are DIFFERENT wire values that hash differently. The validator does not protect you here — JSON Schema treats any number with a zero fractional part as an integer, so 100.0 is accepted and silently journaled with the float shape it arrived in.

notes.description: The notes to add, at least one. Each entry carries its own caller-minted noteId plus start, length, pitch and velocity. One call is ONE journal entry, so a whole chord adds and undoes as a unit.

commands.description: Add a batch of MIDI notes to a note-backed clip in one journal entry. Rejected on an audio clip. NOT self-inverse: undoing an add is a removal, so inverseRule is explicit (note.remove).

commands.name: note.remove

clipId.description: Id of the note-backed clip the notes live in. Rejected on an audio clip.

items.description: Note identity, unique within its clip. Minted UI-SIDE (ULID-shaped), exactly like autopoint.add's pointId — the engine never mints an id at apply time, because a minted id would make replay diverge from the live model.

noteIds.description: The batch this command acts on. One chord drag is ONE journal entry, so relative offsets inside the selection are a property of the command rather than the caller's responsibility.

commands.description: Remove a batch of MIDI notes from a note-backed clip. NOT self-inverse: the removed notes' full state has to come back, so the inverse is a single note.add carrying it.

commands.name: note.move

clipId.description: Id of the note-backed clip the batch lives in. Rejected on an audio clip.

items.description: Note identity, unique within its clip. Minted UI-SIDE (ULID-shaped), exactly like autopoint.add's pointId — the engine never mints an id at apply time, because a minted id would make replay diverge from the live model.

noteIds.description: The batch this command acts on. One chord drag is ONE journal entry, so relative offsets inside the selection are a property of the command rather than the caller's responsibility.

deltaTicks.description: Signed time offset applied to every note in the batch.

deltaPitch.description: Signed semitone offset applied to every note in the batch, -127 to 127. No clamping: if any note would leave 0..127 the whole command is refused.

commands.description: Move a batch of notes in time and/or pitch (the piano-roll drag). DELTA-based, so the inverse is simply the negated delta and relative voicing inside the selection is preserved by construction. The engine does NOT clamp: if the batch would move any note out of range the WHOLE command is refused with a typed error and nothing is applied. Clamping here would break self-inversion (clamp then negate the delta does not return the original) and would collapse a chord onto the boundary note by note; group-clamping that preserves voicing is the caller's job.

commands.name: note.resize

clipId.description: Id of the note-backed clip the batch lives in. Rejected on an audio clip.

items.description: Note identity, unique within its clip. Minted UI-SIDE (ULID-shaped), exactly like autopoint.add's pointId — the engine never mints an id at apply time, because a minted id would make replay diverge from the live model.

noteIds.description: The batch this command acts on. One chord drag is ONE journal entry, so relative offsets inside the selection are a property of the command rather than the caller's responsibility.

edge.description: leading moves the note start and shortens by the same amount; trailing changes the length only.

deltaTicks.description: Signed length/start offset. Positive on the leading edge shortens from the front; positive on the trailing edge lengthens.

commands.description: Resize a batch of notes from one edge. DELTA-based and self-inverse (same edge, negated delta). The engine does NOT clamp: if the batch would move any note out of range the WHOLE command is refused with a typed error and nothing is applied. Clamping here would break self-inversion (clamp then negate the delta does not return the original) and would collapse a chord onto the boundary note by note; group-clamping that preserves voicing is the caller's job.

commands.name: note.velocity.set

clipId.description: Id of the note-backed clip the batch lives in. Rejected on an audio clip.

items.description: Note identity, unique within its clip. Minted UI-SIDE (ULID-shaped), exactly like autopoint.add's pointId — the engine never mints an id at apply time, because a minted id would make replay diverge from the live model.

noteIds.description: The batch this command acts on. One chord drag is ONE journal entry, so relative offsets inside the selection are a property of the command rather than the caller's responsibility.

deltaVelocity.description: Signed velocity offset applied to every note in the batch, -127 to 127. Integer, so the journaled Num shape is stable by construction. No clamping: if any note would leave 0..127 the whole command is refused.

commands.description: Nudge the velocity of a batch of notes by a signed integer offset. Named .set for symmetry with the rest of the catalog; the parameter is a DELTA, which is what makes it self-inverse. The engine does NOT clamp: if the batch would move any note out of range the WHOLE command is refused with a typed error and nothing is applied. Clamping here would break self-inversion (clamp then negate the delta does not return the original) and would collapse a chord onto the boundary note by note; group-clamping that preserves voicing is the caller's job.

commands.name: note.duplicate

clipId.description: Id of the note-backed clip the batch lives in. Rejected on an audio clip.

items.description: Note identity, unique within its clip. Minted UI-SIDE (ULID-shaped), exactly like autopoint.add's pointId — the engine never mints an id at apply time, because a minted id would make replay diverge from the live model.

noteIds.description: The batch this command acts on. One chord drag is ONE journal entry, so relative offsets inside the selection are a property of the command rather than the caller's responsibility.

items.description: Note identity, unique within its clip. Minted UI-SIDE (ULID-shaped), exactly like autopoint.add's pointId — the engine never mints an id at apply time, because a minted id would make replay diverge from the live model.

newNoteIds.description: Ids for the copies, positionally paired with noteIds and the same length. Minted UI-side.

deltaTicks.description: Signed time offset applied to the copies.

deltaPitch.description: Signed semitone offset applied to the copies, -127 to 127. No clamping: if any copy would leave 0..127 the whole command is refused.

commands.description: Copy a batch of notes at a time/pitch offset, using caller-minted ids. NOT self-inverse: undoing a duplicate removes the copies, so inverseRule is explicit (note.remove). The engine does NOT clamp: if the batch would move any note out of range the WHOLE command is refused with a typed error and nothing is applied. Clamping here would break self-inversion (clamp then negate the delta does not return the original) and would collapse a chord onto the boundary note by note; group-clamping that preserves voicing is the caller's job.

commands.name: note.timing.set

clipId.description: Id of the note-backed clip the batch lives in. Rejected on an audio clip.

noteId.description: An EXISTING note in this clip. This command never creates or removes a note; note.add / note.remove own that.

startTicks.description: Absolute clip-relative position, not a delta.

lengthTicks.description: Absolute sounding length in ticks, not a delta. Must be > 0.

notes.description: One entry per note. Every noteId must be distinct and must already exist in the clip.

commands.description: Set the ABSOLUTE start and length of a batch of notes. The one note command that is not delta-shaped, and it exists for exactly one reason: an inverse that has to restore per-note positions no single delta describes. note.quantize names it as its inverse. Self-inverse because the inverse is the same command carrying the pre-state values, the clip.move pattern. Pitch and velocity are untouched: this command is about TIME only, so it can never silently retune a chord.

commands.name: note.quantize

clipId.description: Id of the note-backed clip the batch lives in. Rejected on an audio clip.

items.description: Note identity, unique within its clip. Minted UI-SIDE (ULID-shaped), exactly like autopoint.add's pointId — the engine never mints an id at apply time, because a minted id would make replay diverge from the live model.

noteIds.description: The batch this command acts on. REQUIRED and non-empty: there is deliberately no "quantize the whole clip" spelling, because quantize is destructive to a performance that was played off the grid on purpose. A caller that means every note enumerates every note.

gridTicks.description: The grid division to pull toward, in ticks (960 = a quarter at PPQ 960, 240 = a sixteenth). Lines are measured from the project's phaseAnchorTicks, so a song with a lead-in quantizes to its real bar 1 rather than to tick 0.

strengthPercent.description: How far each note travels toward its grid line, as an INTEGER percent. 100 is mechanical; 50-80 tightens the timing while keeping the feel. Integer rather than a 0..1 float because journaled values are Num and the hash chain depends on their integer/float shape (0.8 and 80 are not interchangeable under canonicalization).

quantizeEnds.description: false: only note STARTS move, lengths are preserved exactly. true: the note END is pulled to the same grid at the same strength, so lengths change. Off is the musical default; legato passages get chopped by an ends-quantize.

commands.description: Pull a batch of notes toward a grid at a given strength. NEVER automatic: nothing in the engine issues this on capture, on import or on load, because the point of a tempo-mapped recording is that the grid was fitted to the performance rather than the other way round. NOT self-inverse and not a delta command: every note moves by its own amount, so the inverse is one note.timing.set carrying the EXACT prior start and length of every note in the batch. Refused whole (nothing applied) if any note would land before tick 0 or, with quantizeEnds, be squeezed below one tick.

commands.name: autolane.show
commands.nonUndoableReason: View-state toggle (whether an automation lane is expanded under a track), not a content mutation.

trackId.description: Id of the track whose automation lane is shown or hidden.

target.description: A ParamRef: dotted ASCII path addressing one automatable parameter. 'track.volume' and 'track.pan' are the reserved v1 spellings and MUST render byte-identically. Unrecognised but well-formed paths are preserved verbatim rather than dropped.

visible.description: true would show the lane, false hide it. NOT IMPLEMENTED in the engine: the command validates trackId and target and returns ok with mutated:false, storing nothing — the Studio UI keeps lane visibility in its own view state, so calling this over the agent surface moves nothing on screen and nothing reads the flag back.

commands.description: Declared as showing or hiding an automation lane in the timeline. The ENGINE stores no such state: this validates the track and the target and returns ok without changing anything, and the Studio UI keeps lane visibility in its own view model. Calling it over the agent surface moves nothing on screen.

commands.name: autopoint.add

trackId.description: Id of the track that owns the lane.

target.description: A ParamRef: dotted ASCII path addressing one automatable parameter. 'track.volume' and 'track.pan' are the reserved v1 spellings and MUST render byte-identically. Unrecognised but well-formed paths are preserved verbatim rather than dropped.

pointId.description: Caller-minted, stable id for the point; the engine never mints one, because a minted id would make replay diverge from the live model. Must be unique on the lane.

positionTicks.description: Where the point sits, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar).

commands.description: Add an automation point on a track parameter lane. v1 automation targets are track.volume and track.pan only.

commands.name: autopoint.move

trackId.description: Id of the track that owns the lane.

target.description: A ParamRef: dotted ASCII path addressing one automatable parameter. 'track.volume' and 'track.pan' are the reserved v1 spellings and MUST render byte-identically. Unrecognised but well-formed paths are preserved verbatim rather than dropped.

pointId.description: Id of an existing point on this lane.

positionTicks.description: New position for the point, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar).

value.description: New value at the point, in the target parameter's OWN units: dB for track.volume, -1..1 for track.pan.

commands.description: Drag an existing automation breakpoint to a new time and/or value. Self-inverse: undo carries the prior position and value.

commands.name: autopoint.remove

trackId.description: Id of the track that owns the lane.

target.description: A ParamRef: dotted ASCII path addressing one automatable parameter. 'track.volume' and 'track.pan' are the reserved v1 spellings and MUST render byte-identically. Unrecognised but well-formed paths are preserved verbatim rather than dropped.

pointId.description: Id of an existing point on this lane.

commands.description: Delete one breakpoint from an automation lane. The lane and its other points stay; use autolane.clear to empty the lane instead.

commands.name: autolane.clear

trackId.description: Id of the track that owns the lane.

target.description: A ParamRef: dotted ASCII path addressing one automatable parameter. 'track.volume' and 'track.pan' are the reserved v1 spellings and MUST render byte-identically. Unrecognised but well-formed paths are preserved verbatim rather than dropped.

commands.description: Remove every automation point on a lane. Undo restores the full prior point set (runtime snapshot, not expressed field-by-field in this schema).

commands.name: mix.gain

trackId.description: Id of the track whose channel fader moves.

gainDb.description: Channel fader in dB, -60 to 12; 0 is unity. The bound is enforced by the executor, not only by this schema.

commands.description: Set a track's mixer channel gain (distinct from clip.setGain, which trims an individual clip).

commands.name: mix.pan

trackId.description: Id of the track whose pan moves.

pan.description: Stereo position, -1 is hard left and 1 is hard right; 0 is centre.

commands.description: Place a track in the stereo field, from hard left to hard right. Distinct from a drum pad's own pan, which device.zone.add carries.

commands.name: mix.eq

trackId.description: Id of the track whose channel EQ changes.

freqHz.description: Band centre frequency in Hz, 20 to 20000. The four bands start at 80, 250, 2500 and 8000 Hz.

gainDb.description: Cut or boost for this band in dB, -24 to 24; 0 is flat.

q.description: Optional bandwidth (resonance): greater than 0, at most 10, higher is narrower. Bands start at 1. OMITTING it leaves the band's stored Q exactly as it was — it is not reset — and the inverse then leaves Q alone too.

commands.description: Move one of the four fixed channel-EQ bands on a track: its frequency, its cut or boost, and optionally its bandwidth. Bands are addressed by index, not created.

commands.name: mix.send

trackId.description: Id of the track being sent from.

bus.description: Which of the two fixed effect returns to feed: 'a' is the REVERB return, 'b' is the DELAY return. Both sum into master.

amount.description: Send level, 0 sends nothing and 1 is unity. LINEAR, not dB.

commands.description: Feed a track into one of the two fixed effect returns — 'a' is the reverb, 'b' is the delay — without routing the track away from master.

commands.name: mix.master.gain

gainDb.description: Master fader in dB, -60 to 12; 0 is unity. The bound is enforced by the executor, not only by this schema.

commands.description: Move the master fader — the last gain stage before the limiter and the file. Reach for this to trim an export that is too hot, rather than pulling every channel down.

commands.name: mix.limiter.set

enabled.description: true engages the master limiter, false bypasses it. Absolute, not a toggle; a new project starts with it off.

ceilingDb.description: Optional output ceiling in dBFS, -6 to 0. A new project starts at -1; OMITTING this leaves the stored ceiling exactly as it was rather than resetting it.

releaseMs.description: Optional release time in milliseconds, 1 to 1000. A new project starts at 50; OMITTING this leaves the stored release exactly as it was rather than resetting it.

commands.description: Enable/disable and configure the master limiter. mute/solo are on track.mute/track.solo, not here.

commands.name: gen.song
commands.nonUndoableReason: Journals the async generation REQUEST only; it does not itself mutate the timeline. The resulting take is placed by a subsequent take.promote, which is the undoable step.

requestId.description: Caller-minted ULID naming this job: Crockford base32, 26 characters, first character 0-7. gen.landed quotes it back and gen.cancel takes it. Mint a fresh one per request.

trackId.description: Id of the track the result is destined for; it must already exist. Nothing is placed by this command — take.promote does that once the take lands.

insertAtTicks.description: Where the result is meant to land, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar). Recorded on the request record; the actual placement happens at take.promote.

caption.description: The text2music prompt, e.g. 'dreamy lo-fi hip hop with rhodes'. Non-empty.

request.description: The rest of the Gen Protocol 'generate' request. caption is the one field this schema pins; the full shape is in gen-protocol.v1.yaml (see gen-protocol-mapping.md).

commands.description: Journal a request for a new text2music generation. RECORDS the request on the bus and returns; it does not itself call a generation backend, and nothing is placed on the timeline until a take lands and take.promote commits it. Gen Protocol op: generate.

commands.name: gen.revise
commands.nonUndoableReason: Journals the async generation REQUEST only.

requestId.description: Caller-minted ULID naming this job: Crockford base32, 26 characters, first character 0-7. Mint a fresh one per request.

clipId.description: Id of the clip whose region is repainted. Must exist.

regionStartTicks.description: Region start, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar). Must be strictly before regionEndTicks — an empty or inverted region is refused.

regionEndTicks.description: Region end, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar). Must be strictly after regionStartTicks.

scope.description: What the repaint touches: the scalar 'all-stems', or one stem name, or an array of stem names from 'vocals', 'drums', 'bass' and 'other'. 'all-stems' is valid only as a scalar; an array selects those stems and null-preserves the rest.

instruction.description: What to change, in words, e.g. 'make the drums busier'. Non-empty.

variants.description: How many alternative takes to ask for, 1 to 5. Default 1.

request.description: The rest of the Gen Protocol 'revise' request. instruction is required and variants optional; the full shape is in gen-protocol.v1.yaml (see gen-protocol-mapping.md).

commands.description: Journal a request to repaint a region of a clip with an instruction delta. RECORDS the request on the bus and returns; it does not itself call a backend. The pipeline tool studio_revise is what actually runs the revise/land/promote sequence. Gen Protocol op: revise.
