commands.name: gen.cancel
commands.nonUndoableReason: Cancellation is not itself invertible.

requestId.description: The requestId of the job to cancel: Crockford base32 ULID, 26 characters, first character 0-7. See this command's own note — the shipped backend cancel is global, not per-request.

commands.description: Cancel an in-flight gen request. KNOWN v1 BACKEND GAP (see gen-protocol-mapping.md): the current Python backend's cancel_generation RPC is a single global cancel flag, not per-job; the Gen Protocol's per-requestId cancel is the target contract, not yet the shipped behavior.

commands.name: gen.finalize
commands.nonUndoableReason: Journals the async re-render REQUEST only; the resulting swap is applied when gen.landed arrives.

requestId.description: Caller-minted ULID naming this re-render job: Crockford base32, 26 characters, first character 0-7. Distinct from the requestId that produced draftTakeId.

draftTakeId.description: The committed draft take being re-rendered at higher quality.

targetQualityRung.description: Quality rung to re-render at: 'draft' (acestep-v15-turbo, 8 steps), 'standard' (acestep-v15-quality) or 'full' (acestep-v15-base, 50 steps). finalize always targets a rung above the draft's own.

request.description: The same request body as the revise op that produced draftTakeId — identical region, instruction and scope. Only the model/steps rung changes. See gen-protocol-mapping.md.

commands.description: Re-render a committed draft take at full quality and splice it in place: same region, same lineage, journaled as a swap. This is the draft/commit re-render swap named in 02-ARCH section 4's gen catalog line.

commands.name: gen.landed
commands.nonUndoableReason: System-authored completion record of an async gen.* request; not itself a user-invocable command.

requestId.description: Matches the requestId of the gen.* command that started this job.

sourceCommand.description: Dotted catalog name of the gen.* command that started this job, e.g. 'gen.revise'. Lineage and the export manifest read it to say which operation produced the take.

takeId.description: Id of the candidate take this job produced. take.promote / take.discard / take.purge address it by this id.

assetHashes.description: The audio this job produced, keyed by 'mix' for a single-file take or by stem name ('vocals', 'drums', 'bass', 'other') for a per-stem take. Each value is a 64-character lowercase blake3 hex hash.

model.description: Model identifier as the backend reports it, e.g. 'acestep-v15-turbo'. Non-empty.

steps.description: Optional diffusion step count, 1 or more. Omitted when the backend does not report it.

seed.description: Optional RNG seed the run used; any integer, negative included. It is what makes a retake reproducible. Omitted when the backend does not report one.

engineIdentity.description: Which engine produced the audio, for lineage and the AI-disclosure manifest: model and device are required, steps and seed are optional and present only when the backend reported them.

latencySeconds.description: Optional wall-clock duration of the job in seconds, 0 or more. Omitted when it was not measured.

commands.description: Written by the engine (actor.kind=system) when any async gen.* request reaches a terminal success state. Carries the provenance the lineage tree and export manifests read: asset hashes + engine identity, per 02-ARCH section 4 ('completion journals gen.landed with asset hashes') and section 5 ('terminal ... with artifact paths + content hashes + engine identity for lineage').

commands.name: take.promote

takeId.description: Id of the candidate take to commit — the takeId gen.landed reported.

targetClipId.description: Clip the take is spliced into; for a new gen.song this may be a clip created as part of promotion.

commands.description: Commit a generated take into the timeline, splicing it into (or creating) a clip. This is the undoable step that actually mutates the visible project; the gen.* request that produced the take is not itself undoable.

commands.name: take.discard

takeId.description: Id of the candidate take to drop from the active list. Its audio stays under takes/ until a purge, so this stays reversible.

commands.description: Discard a generated take. The take's asset stays under takes/ until the user purges it (section 6); discard only removes it from the active candidate list, so it remains reversible.

commands.name: take.purge

takeId.description: Id of an UN-PROMOTED candidate take to mark offline so its audio can be reclaimed. Manage tier: the tool also needs confirm: true.

commands.description: Mark an un-promoted candidate take offline so its unreferenced audio may be reclaimed. The journaled state change preserves lineage and is undoable.

commands.name: take.restore

takeId.description: Id of an offline take to bring back to candidate status. Only the journal state is restored — the audio may need regeneration before it can be auditioned.

commands.description: Restore an offline candidate take's journal state after undoing take.purge. Audio reclamation is host-managed and may require regeneration or recovery before audition.

commands.name: take.auditionMix
commands.nonUndoableReason: Preview/listening action (which per-stem take is heard while auditioning), not a committed mutation.

takeId.description: Id of the per-stem take being auditioned. Must be a take this project knows.

stems.description: Which stems should be audible: at least one of 'vocals', 'drums', 'bass', 'other', 'mix'. NOT IMPLEMENTED: the executor checks takeId, ignores this list entirely and returns ok with mutated:false. Nothing in the engine stores or reads it, so what you hear does not change.

commands.description: Declared as choosing which stems of a per-stem take are audible while auditioning. NOT IMPLEMENTED: the executor checks the takeId, ignores the stem list and returns ok with mutated:false, so nothing changes about what you hear.

commands.name: import.audio

sourcePath.description: Filesystem path of the audio file to bring in. It is COPIED content-addressed into the package's audio/ directory, so the original may move afterwards.

targetTrackId.description: Id of the existing track the imported clip is placed on.

separate.description: Declared as 'run htdemucs on import and place stems as separate tracks'. NOT IMPLEMENTED and silently ignored: the file is imported and placed as one ordinary clip. Use studio_open_in_studio for separation, or import.stems with stems you separated yourself. Default false.

conform.description: Declared as 'time-stretch the imported audio to the project tempo on import'. NOT IMPLEMENTED and silently ignored: the audio is imported at its own length. Default false. To fit it to the tempo, place it and then call clip.warp.set.

startTicks.description: Optional clip start on the target track, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar). Default 0.

clipId.description: Optional caller-minted id for the placed clip. Omitted, the host mints one and returns it in the result.

commands.description: Import an external audio file, copy it content-addressed into audio/, and place it as a clip.

commands.name: import.stems

sourceDir.description: Filesystem path of a directory of stem files. Every audio file directly in it is copied content-addressed into audio/ and placed on its own track.

targetTrackId.description: Id of the FIRST track of the group; the remaining stems land on tracks created after it.

startTicks.description: Optional common start for every stem, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar). Default 0, which keeps the stems aligned with each other.

groupName.description: Optional label for the imported group, echoed back in the result. Defaults to 'Imported stems'.

commands.description: Bring a folder of stem files in as one aligned track per stem, each copied content-addressed into audio/. This is the working multi-track import — studio.importStemSession is not.

commands.name: export.master
commands.nonUndoableReason: Export writes a file outside the project package; it does not mutate project content. Per 02-ARCH section 4's acceptance hook, export.* is journaled (provenance: what was exported, when, from which state) but explicitly non-undoable, same as transport.

outputPath.description: Filesystem path to write the bounce to, file name included. Manage tier: this writes outside the project, so the tool also needs confirm: true.

format.description: Deliverable format. 'wav' (24-bit at the project rate) and 'aac' (AAC-LC via Apple AudioToolbox) are what this build writes; 'flac' is in the enum but the exporter REFUSES it with a typed Unsupported error — it lands with the IO codec pass.

sampleRateHz.description: Optional output rate. The enum admits 44100 and 48000, but v1 always exports at the PROJECT rate and refuses any value that differs from it, so the only value accepted is whichever of the two the project already runs at. Omit unless you are asserting that rate.

loudnessTarget.description: Optional EBU R128 integrated-LUFS normalization for the master: 'streaming' (-14), 'club' (-7), 'broadcast' (-16), or 'none'. Omitted or 'none' writes the mix exactly as bounced.

includeManifest.description: Optional. true also writes the AI-disclosure provenance manifest next to the audio (<output>.manifest.json). Omitted is false.

commands.description: Bounce the full master mix to a file, via the render graph's offline path (same graph as realtime, per 02-ARCH section 3). WAV is 24-bit at the project rate; AAC via Apple AudioToolbox. Optional loudness target + provenance manifest (L13).

commands.name: export.stems
commands.nonUndoableReason: Export writes files outside the project package; see export.master.

outputDir.description: Directory to write one file per track into; created if missing. Manage tier: the tool also needs confirm: true.

format.description: Stem format. Only 'wav' (24-bit, project rate, never loudness-normalized) is written; 'flac' is in the enum but the exporter refuses anything that is not wav with a typed Unsupported error.

stems.description: Declared as a filter over the four separated stems 'vocals', 'drums', 'bass' and 'other'. NOT IMPLEMENTED and optional in every sense: the exporter ignores it and always writes one WAV per TRACK, whether it is present or omitted.

includeManifest.description: Optional. true also writes the AI-disclosure provenance manifest next to the stems (stems.manifest.json). Omitted is false.

commands.description: Bounce one 24-bit WAV per TRACK into a directory, at the project rate and without loudness normalization. The declared 'stems' filter and the 'flac' format are not implemented; see those parameters.

commands.name: export.region
commands.nonUndoableReason: Export writes a file outside the project package; see export.master.

outputPath.description: Filesystem path to write the region bounce to, file name included. Manage tier: this writes outside the project, so the tool also needs confirm: true.

startTicks.description: Region start, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar).

endTicks.description: Region end, in absolute timeline ticks from 0 (PPQ 960: 960 ticks is a quarter note, 3840 is one 4/4 bar); must be after startTicks.

format.description: Deliverable format. 'wav' (24-bit at the project rate) and 'aac' (AAC-LC via Apple AudioToolbox) are what this build writes; 'flac' is in the enum but the exporter REFUSES it with a typed Unsupported error.

loudnessTarget.description: Optional EBU R128 integrated-LUFS normalization for the region: 'streaming' (-14), 'club' (-7), 'broadcast' (-16), or 'none'. Omitted or 'none' writes the region exactly as bounced.

includeManifest.description: Optional. true also writes the AI-disclosure provenance manifest next to the audio (<output>.manifest.json). Omitted is false.

commands.description: Bounce a time region of the master mix to a file (24-bit WAV or AAC). Optional loudness target + provenance manifest (L13).

commands.name: export.manifest
commands.nonUndoableReason: Export writes a file outside the project package; see export.master.

outputPath.description: Filesystem path to write the provenance manifest JSON to. Manage tier: this writes outside the project, so the tool also needs confirm: true. Use the studio_manifest READ tool if you only want to look at it.

commands.description: Write the provenance manifest (rebuildable view over the journal, per section 6) to a standalone file.

commands.name: publish.track
commands.nonUndoableReason: Publishes to majiks.online, an external system; not a local project mutation.

assetHash.description: blake3 hash of the already-exported asset to publish: 64 lowercase hex characters, the same spelling clip.place's assetHash uses.

title.description: Title the track is published under. Non-empty.

metadata.description: Optional free-form metadata object handed to the publish pipeline unchanged. No shape is enforced here, and this build records it rather than sending it.

commands.description: Journal the intent to publish an exported asset with its provenance certificate. The engine surface RECORDS this and returns executed:false — the majiks.online pipeline itself is the app's, shipped pre-Studio and out of this surface's scope.

commands.name: txn.begin
commands.nonUndoableReason: Structural bracket marker, not a content mutation itself. Atomicity applies to the journaled commands between this and the matching txn.commit (02-ARCH section 4: 'Multi-op user gestures wrap in txn.begin/txn.commit (atomic undo unit)'); undoing the group is driven by walking that bracketed range, not by inverting txn.begin directly.

txnId.description: Caller-minted, stable id for the transaction; txn.commit must quote the same one. v1 does not nest — exactly one txnId may be open at a time.

reason.description: Optional human-readable label for the unit of work, e.g. 'drag 3 clips'. Shown in undo history; omitted leaves it unlabelled.

commands.description: Open an atomic transaction: journaled commands until the matching txn.commit undo/redo as one unit. v1 transactions do not nest (one open txnId at a time).

commands.name: txn.commit
commands.nonUndoableReason: Structural bracket marker; see txn.begin.

txnId.description: The txnId of the open transaction to close. It must match a preceding txn.begin that is still open.

commands.description: Close the atomic transaction opened by the txn.begin with the same txnId. Conformance checks that every txn.commit has a preceding, matching, not-yet-closed txn.begin.

commands.name: studio.importStemSession

stemSessionId.description: Id of the Stem Sessions session to bring in. In this build it is used ONLY to mint a placeholder track ('trk_stems_<id>', named 'Stem Session <id>'): no session is looked up, no audio is copied and no clips are created.

commands.description: Declared as bringing a Stem Sessions multitrack session onto the timeline as tracks+clips. What it actually does in this build is add ONE empty placeholder track named after the id — no session is looked up, no audio is copied, no clips are created. import.stems is the working multi-track import. Flag v1.1.

commands.name: project.setPhaseAnchor

anchorTicks.description: Ticks the project bar grid is shifted by, so the first tracked downbeat lands on a bar line without a lead-in. 0 is the v1 behaviour.

commands.description: Set the project-level phase anchor for the bar grid (L8 proposal). Warp markers (E7) and stem lead-in alignment both read it.

commands.name: route.node.add

nodeId.description: Opaque id. Must not contain '.' so node refs stay parseable.

kind.description: What kind of node this is: 'bus' (an aux/effect destination fed by sends) or 'group' (a submix whose members route into it instead of straight to master).

name.description: Display name for the bus or group, e.g. 'Drum Bus'. Non-empty; nodeId, not this, is the wire identity.

commands.description: Add a routing node (bus or group) to the project routing graph. Track strips and master are implicit nodes and are never added or removed here.

commands.name: route.node.remove

nodeId.description: Id of the bus/group node to remove. Every edge touching it is removed too, and undo restores the node with all of them.

commands.description: Remove a routing node and every edge incident to it. Undo restores the node and all removed edges (multi-command inverse; the catalog hint is the declared route.node.add).

commands.name: route.connect

edgeId.description: Caller-minted, stable id for the new edge: letters, digits, '_' and '-' only, never '.'. Must not already be in use.

level.description: Linear send level for the new edge, 0 (silent) to 4; 1 is unity. Linear, not dB.

tap.description: Where the source is tapped: 'pre' (before its fader, so the send is independent of the fader) or 'post' (after it).

commands.description: Connect two routing nodes. Rejected at command time if the edge would create a cycle, so the audio thread can never discover one.

commands.name: route.disconnect

edgeId.description: Id of the edge to remove. Undo re-creates it with the same level and tap.

commands.description: Delete one edge from the routing graph, silencing that path. Undo re-creates the edge with the level and tap it had, so this is the safe way to try a routing change.

commands.name: route.edge.set

level.description: Linear send level, 0 (silent) to 4; 1 is unity. Linear, not dB.

tap.description: Where the source is tapped: 'pre' (before its fader, so the send is independent of the fader) or 'post' (after it, so the fader rides the send too).

commands.description: Set an existing routing edge's level and tap. Both are required so the self-inverse restores the exact prior edge state.

commands.name: route.node.set

nodeId.description: Id of the bus/group node whose fader moves. Track strips and master are not addressable here — mix.gain and mix.master.gain own those.

gainDb.description: Node fader in dB, -60 to 12; 0 is unity. When a bus.<nodeId>.gain automation lane exists, the lane value wins for the rendered gain and this is the static fallback.

commands.description: Set a routing node's (bus or group) fader gain in dB — the node fader of DESIGN-E5-routing.md §4.3. The static half of the same fader the bus.<nodeId>.gain automation lane drives (when that lane exists, the lane value takes precedence for the rendered gain). Self-inverse carries the prior gain.

commands.name: fx.add

target.description: The fx HOST, as a NodeRef: 'track.<id>', 'bus.<id>' or 'master'. Master is addressable because a master-bus effect chain is table stakes for parity and falls out of the NodeRef grammar for free.

fxId.description: Opaque fx id, unique within this host's chain. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef paths track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey>, bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> and master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> stay parseable.

kind.description: Which effect to insert, from the CLOSED E5 vocabulary: 'eq', 'compressor', 'gate', 'delay', 'reverb', 'saturator', 'chorus', 'utility' or 'limiter'. An unknown kind fails loudly at the contract boundary rather than building a silent no-op node.

commands.description: Append an effect to the insert chain on a track, a bus/group node, or master. A SEPARATE registry from device.add, whose 'kind' enum is NOT widened: build_instrument hard-errors on a track with more than one device, so an effect in Track.devices would break the compile of every instrument track that also carries an effect. Its parameters become automatable IMMEDIATELY through track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> / bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> / master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> - no catalog schema change, because the autopoint/autolane target pattern already admits them. A NEW command name (E0 9.2).

commands.name: fx.remove

target.description: The fx HOST, as a NodeRef: 'track.<id>', 'bus.<id>' or 'master'. Master is addressable because a master-bus effect chain is table stakes for parity and falls out of the NodeRef grammar for free.

fxId.description: Opaque fx id, unique within this host's chain. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef paths track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey>, bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> and master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> stay parseable.

commands.description: Remove an effect from an insert chain. Undo restores the effect, its chain index, every stored parameter and its sidechain link - a multi-command inverse; the catalog hint is the declared fx.add. Unlike device.remove this refuses nothing for stored parameters: fx.param.set can restore them, so the guard device.remove needs would only make every configured effect unremovable. Refused only if the effect carries unknown fields no command in this build can restore.

commands.name: fx.move

target.description: The fx HOST, as a NodeRef: 'track.<id>', 'bus.<id>' or 'master'. Master is addressable because a master-bus effect chain is table stakes for parity and falls out of the NodeRef grammar for free.

fxId.description: Opaque fx id, unique within this host's chain. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef paths track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey>, bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> and master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> stay parseable.

index.description: New 0-based position in the chain. Chain order IS processing order.

commands.description: Reorder one effect within its insert chain. Self-inverse: the inverse carries the prior index, and remove+insert is a rotation whose reverse restores exactly.

commands.name: fx.param.set

target.description: The fx HOST, as a NodeRef: 'track.<id>', 'bus.<id>' or 'master'. Master is addressable because a master-bus effect chain is table stakes for parity and falls out of the NodeRef grammar for free.

fxId.description: Opaque fx id, unique within this host's chain. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef paths track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey>, bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> and master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> stay parseable.

key.description: An effect parameter key from FX_PARAM_KEYS. Which keys a given kind honours is deliberately NOT validated: apply.rs runs on replay, so tightening the (kind, key) pairing later would break replay of a project that automated a key its kind ignores. A lane bound to an ignored key is surfaced by CompileReport.inert_lanes instead.

value.description: Parameter value. Journaled as a Num, so the integer/float SHAPE round-trips exactly.

commands.description: Set one effect parameter. Parameters stay SPARSE: an absent key means the DSP default, exactly as build_instrument already implements it, so no default is ever materialized into the project. inverseShape is 'multi' because the declared inverse name cannot cover both directions - the real inverse is a fx.param.set carrying the prior value, OR a fx.param.clear when the key was absent, so an undo returns the key to ABSENT rather than to a written default. This is the parameter setter E1/E2 deliberately omitted for Device; E5 is the DSP lane and can supply the semantics E1/E2 could not.

commands.name: fx.param.clear

target.description: The fx HOST, as a NodeRef: 'track.<id>', 'bus.<id>' or 'master'. Master is addressable because a master-bus effect chain is table stakes for parity and falls out of the NodeRef grammar for free.

fxId.description: Opaque fx id, unique within this host's chain. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef paths track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey>, bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> and master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> stay parseable.

key.description: An effect parameter key from FX_PARAM_KEYS. Which keys a given kind honours is deliberately NOT validated: apply.rs runs on replay, so tightening the (kind, key) pairing later would break replay of a project that automated a key its kind ignores. A lane bound to an ignored key is surfaced by CompileReport.inert_lanes instead.

commands.description: Drop one stored effect parameter, restoring sparsity so the key reads as the DSP default again. Clearing a key that stores no value is a typed error, not a silent no-op: a no-op has no exact inverse to journal.

commands.name: fx.sidechain.set

target.description: The fx HOST, as a NodeRef: 'track.<id>', 'bus.<id>' or 'master'. Master is addressable because a master-bus effect chain is table stakes for parity and falls out of the NodeRef grammar for free.

fxId.description: Opaque fx id, unique within this host's chain. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef paths track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey>, bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> and master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> stay parseable.

source.description: The KEY source, as a NodeRef: 'track.<id>' or 'bus.<id>'. Master is the sink and can never be a key source.

commands.description: Key an effect's detector from another node. A sidechain is an ORDERING CONSTRAINT, not an audio edge: it creates no routing edge and contributes no audio, but the source must be scheduled before the host or the detector reads a not-yet-written accumulator - exactly 0.0, i.e. silence, not a small error. Rejected at command time if the source does not resolve, is the host itself (that is the internal detector, not a link), is master, or would create a cycle over edges and links together. inverseShape is 'multi' because the inverse is a set-to-prior OR a clear.

commands.name: fx.sidechain.clear

target.description: The fx HOST, as a NodeRef: 'track.<id>', 'bus.<id>' or 'master'. Master is addressable because a master-bus effect chain is table stakes for parity and falls out of the NodeRef grammar for free.

fxId.description: Opaque fx id, unique within this host's chain. Must not contain '.' so the ParamRef paths track.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey>, bus.<nodeId>.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> and master.fx.<fxId>.<paramKey> stay parseable.

commands.description: Return an effect's detector to its internal (self) key. Clearing an effect that has no link is a typed error, not a silent no-op.
